old_title: Ukraine war live: Trump team admits Patriot missiles may not have been delivered
new_title: Ukraine war latest: Trump celebrates release of US prisoner in Russia

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that it could be accurate that a batch of vital interceptor missiles headed for Ukraine has not been delivered.
The Patriot missiles, which have provided a vital lifeline to Ukrainian cities in defending against Russian aerial attacks, were purchased by under the PURL programme, which lets Nato allies by aid from the US for Ukraine.
"I think the important takeaway for you is that there has not been some deliberate political directive to go out and harm Ukraine," Rubio emphasised in comments to reporters.
A source earlier told Reuters that defence secretary Pete Hegseth has yet to authorise the delivery of the latest package of US weaponry purchased through PURL. It was unclear if that shipment included the Patriots.
The relationship between the US and Ukraine has nosedived in recent weeks, after Donald Trump announced a deal to purchase Russian diesel and lifted sanctions in a bid to lower fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.
Zelensky was due to meet with US special envoy Steve Witkoff in a bid to repair the relationship, but has in recent days claimed the US is still restricting intelligence sharing.
Zelensky to meet Witkoff in Oslo
Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky will fly to Oslo to meet US special envoy Steve Witkoff on Tuesday, trying to repair ties with Washington that have deteriorated sharply over the past two weeks as president Donald Trump has increasingly courted Moscow.
Trump, who has waived sanctions on Russia in what he says is an effort to lower US fuel prices, has repeatedly rebuked Zelensky. Kyiv says Washington has lately failed to provide early warning notification of Russian missile launches, and has throttled SpaceX satellite links that guide Ukrainian drones.
On Monday, Trump said "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine" and "Zelensky is not helping matters much". He called on Kyiv to find "somebody else to negotiate".
Zelensky said he had spoken with secretary of state Marco Rubio on issues including ballistic missile interceptors, early warning of Russian missile attacks and "the situation with Starlink/Starshield, which needs to be restored", referring to the SpaceX satellite system.
"Of course, all of this comes against the backdrop of our diplomatic efforts to end this horrific war and the constant killing of people," Zelensky said in a post on X.
South Korea to withdraw some embassy staff from Ukraine
South Korea on Tuesday said it will withdraw some staff from its embassy in Kyiv, deepening a diplomatic row over Ukraine's announcement last month of a transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war that Seoul says was meant to be secret.
The diplomatic dispute between the countries began after Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky disclosed the prisoners' transfer during a 23 September speech at the United Nations. South Korea has accused Ukraine of violating a nondisclosure agreement, but Ukraine denies the countries reached such a deal, further angering Seoul.
South Korea recalled its ambassador to Ukraine earlier this month in protest. Ukrainian foreign ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi told local media at the time that Kyiv remains open to "constructive dialogue" and that "diplomacy must prevail over emotions".
South Korean foreign ministry spokesperson Park Doosoon said that the withdrawal of additional embassy staff was due to Ukraine's "lack of constructive steps" to address Seoul's grievances as well as concerns about safety amid intensifying Russian attacks.
What should the UK and Europe do as Trump abandons West?
Trump's plan for talks about Ukraine in China without Ukraine is the latest in his sabotage campaign for Vladimir Putin, writes world affairs editor Sam Kiley - and Europe and the UK need to act.
Russia says it hit cargo vessels and logistics hubs in Ukraine
The Russian military struck three cargo vessels in Ukraine's port of Reni and another cargo vessel en route to Odesa, the Russian defence ministry said on Telegram.
It also said it hit two logistics hubs in the Volyn region and in the city of Khmelnitskiy.
The Russian defence ministry claimed all the vessels and the logistics hubs were being used for military purposes.
Zelensky travels to Norway for talks on war and security
Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky is arriving in Oslo on Tuesday for talks on the war in Ukraine and European security, the Norwegian government and co-host Finland said.
Reuters reported on Monday that US president Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff will travel to Norway this week for a round of negotiations on ending the war in Ukraine, and that Zelensky and European representatives were expected to attend.
"President Zelensky has asked Norway and Finland to arrange a meeting as part of ongoing diplomatic efforts, at a critical time for Ukraine," Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Stoere said in a statement.
Finland's president Alexander Stubb said he will attend meetings with Zelensky and Stoere to discuss "Russia's illegal war of aggression against Ukraine and the overall security situation in Europe".
Zelensky, Stubb and Stoere will hold a press conference later on Tuesday, Norway said.
The statements from Norway and Finland made no mention of any US or European delegations.
Russian airstrike kills three in Kyiv region
An overnight Russian airstrike killed three people and injured another six in the region surrounding Ukraine's capital of Kyiv, the area's emergency service said on Telegram on Tuesday.
Russian forces struck a production and warehouse building where a fire was later extinguished, the emergency service said in the post.
Belarus bars entry to some goods from Latvia
Belarus, one of Russia's closest allies, said on Monday it was barring the entry of a number of goods from neighbouring Latvia because of the Baltic state's "unfriendly" relations.
Belarus's government had slapped the ban on a range of products including canned fish and various industrial goods, state news agency Belta said.
"This decision was taken in connection with the Latvian side maintaining an unconstructive approach and unfriendly rhetoric in relation to Belarus," Belta quoted the government decision as saying.
Latvia closed its border with Belarus in July.
Like Belarus's other neighbours, Latvia has encountered difficulties with Minsk over mass attempts by migrants to cross the Belarusian border into the European Union.
Belarus denies colluding or encouraging migrants from other countries to attempt to cross its borders into the EU.
Led by president Alexander Lukashenko since 1994, Belarus has long been accused of human rights abuses subject to Western sanctions. Lukashenko allowed Russia to use Belarusian territory to help launch the 2022 invasion of Ukraine but has declined to commit his country's forces to the conflict.
US yet to authorise delivery of latest Nato weaponry package to Ukraine - sources
Secretary of defence Pete Hegseth has yet to authorise delivery of the latest package of US weaponry purchased by Nato allies under a program known as PURL, a source told Reuters.
The source could not confirm whether the shipment included Patriots.
The relationship between the US and Ukraine has nosedived in recent weeks, after Donald Trump announced a deal to purchase Russian diesel and temporarily waived some sanctions in a bid to lower fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections.
The US president has accused Zelensky of refusing to hold peace talks with Russia and in his latest broadside on Monday said that maybe it was time that the Ukrainian leader "get somebody else to negotiate." Zelensky has consistently said he is ready for talks.
US officials plan to travel to Norway, Russia for Ukraine talks, say sources
US president Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to travel to Norway this week for the next round of negotiations on ending the war in Ukraine, according to three people familiar with the matter.
Two of the people said they expected Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky to attend the meetings. Another person familiar with the matter said Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, who was expected to take part in the talks, was sick and would attend virtually.
The Oslo discussions are expected to include Zelensky, Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Store, representatives of the E4 - made up of Britain, France, Germany, and Poland - the European Union, and Nato.
Witkoff is also set to travel to Russia to meet president Vladimir Putin, two of the people familiar with the matter said. The Russian conversations are going to focus on a range of topics related to Ukraine as well as the release of American citizen Stephen Hubbard, who was jailed in Russia in 2022.
Senators hold call with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky
Senators who organised a call with Volodymyr Zelensky said he confirmed that critical Starlink services remain degraded, impeding Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones.
Republican senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina and Democratic senator Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut said in a statement that Zelensky also reported disruptions to US intelligence sharing concerning early warning of Russian ballistic missile launches.
"As a result of these disruptions, civilians - children - are dying," the senators said.
The senators participated in the call after the Trump administration waived sanctions against Russia approved recently by Congress.
The senators said that Democrats and Republicans understand what will happen if Russian president Vladimir Putin faces no consequences, and they remain committed to Ukraine and European allies trying to end "the slaughter in Russia's war of aggression".
"Zelensky reiterated his willingness to halt strikes on Russian energy facilities as President Trump has proposed, but only if Putin agrees to the same - a fair request," they said.

Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social to celebrate Vladimir Putin's decision to release Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen who was formally designated as wrongfully detained in Russia for four years.
Mr Hubbard's release came after Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in St Petersburg for talks with Russian president Vladimir Putin on ending the Ukraine war.
Witkoff has come straight from Norway, where he met with Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky in a bid to stabilise worsening relations between Kyiv and Washington.
In televised remarks at the beginning of his meeting with Putin, Witkoff said his goal was to discuss the resumption of trilateral talks involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
He said a resumption of talks would allow technical teams to discuss the next steps toward a peace settlement.
Meanwhile, a Wall Street Journal report said it was Elon Musk who ordered the slowdown of Ukraine's access to his military-grade Starlink satellite internet, which is critical for Kyiv's attack and defence drone capabilities. Musk has previously claimed such decisions are down to the military and the president.
South Korea to recall some of its diplomats from Kyiv
South Korea will withdraw some of its diplomatic personnel from Ukraine amid worsening relations between Seoul and Kyiv over the disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs), Yonhap news agency reported, citing Seoul's foreign ministry.
"This measure was taken because we judged it necessary to facilitate an amicable resolution of the issue and restore trust between the two countries," foreign ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon said, according to Yonhap.
The move follows South Korea's decision to recall its ambassador to Ukraine on 8 October after Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky publicly disclosed the transfer of the two prisoners to South Korea during his speech at the UN General Assembly on 23 September.
Seoul claims the announcement violated a confidentiality agreement between the two countries.
Trump hails Putin for releasing US citizen Stephen Hubbard
Donald Trump has posted on Truth Social to celebrate Vladimir Putin's decision to release Stephen Hubbard, a US citizen who was formally designated as wrongfully detained in Russia for four years.
"Stephen is on his way back home and will soon be with his family. The United States, out of respect for President Trump, was not required to give anything in return - an unprecedented situation for Russia," the post read.
Hubbard's release comes after a number of US concessions towards Russia in recent weeks, including a deal signed by Trump to obtain diesel from Moscow.
Nonetheless, Trump claimed that "there was no 'swap' necessary for this release".
"Welcome home Stephen, it's great to have you back," the statement quoted Trump as saying.
Trump's envoy says he hopes to restart three-way talks with Russia and Ukraine
In televised remarks at the beginning of his meeting with Vladimir Putin, Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff said his goal was to discuss the resumption of trilateral talks involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
He said a resumption of talks would allow technical teams to discuss the next steps toward a peace settlement.
Witkoff and Putin met at St Petersburg's Constantine Palace, with Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev and Putin's foreign affairs adviser Yuri Ushakov also at the table. Witkoff said Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner would join the discussion via a video link.
Witkoff said he would inform Putin about Tuesday's talks in Oslo, which he described as "productive," adding that "there is some degree of momentum."
He thanked Putin for lifting Russia's ban on diesel exports, which angered some US lawmakers, adding that it would help reduce prices for US farmers and truckers.
Putin thanked Trump and Witkoff for their efforts to end the war and said he was ready to discuss restoring US-Russian economic ties.
Putin was also due to meet later on Wednesday with Chinese premier Li Qiang, who is in St Petersburg meeting with other Russian top officials, the Kremlin said.
'I lay in a pool of blood after being shot at point blank range while undercover in Northern Ireland'
A former member of one of the British Army's most secret surveillance units has, for the first time, told the dramatic story of his role in an undercover operation that ended with him being shot through the stomach, his partner mortally wounded, and a wanted IRA gunman fleeing injured into the night.
The veteran, known only as Blue*, recounted how events unfolded in episode five of SAS: The Shadow War.
He was just 22 and serving with 14 Intelligence Company - the clandestine unit known simply as "the Det" - when he and another soldier set up a covert observation post beside a farm in South Derry on St Patrick's Day, 17 March 1978.
Putin says he and Trump could meet in China
Russian president Vladimir Putin proposed meeting US president Donald Trump in China during talks with Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg.
Both US and Russian officials have confirmed in recent days that a possible three-way summit in China was being discussed, but this is the first time Putin has raised the prospect personally.
Any meeting would likely take place on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China next month, which Trump is already due to attend.
Putin also offered to talkabout restoring economic cooperation between Moscow and Washington, Russian state TV said.
Putin tells Witkoff that Russia is releasing US citizen Stephen Hubbard
Russia has released retired American teacher Stephen Hubbard, who had been imprisoned on charges of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine, US envoy Steve Witkoff says.
Witkoff is meeting today with Russian president Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg. He says Putin told him that Hubbard was at the St Petersburg airport, Pulkovo, after his release.
Stephen Hubbard, of Michigan, was sentenced after a closed trial in 2024 to nearly seven years in prison. Prosecutors said he had signed a contract with the Ukrainian military after Russia sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022, and that he fought alongside them until being captured two months later.
The US government under the Biden administration designated Hubbard as wrongfully detained.
Rubio says Zelensky and Witkoff's meeting was 'positive'
US secretary of state Marco Rubio says special envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky a day earlier had been "positive", with nothing "unexpected" or "surprising".
"He (Witkoff) will now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St Petersburg and share them with the Russian side, and let's see if we can make some progress," Rubio told reporters in Mumbai today, where he is taking part in a two-day visit to India.
Pictures show a missile crater in Kharkiv after two killed
Pictures have shown the scale of damage in Kharkiv after overnight Russian drone strikes killed two people.
Regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said on Telegram on Wednesday another 11 people suffered stress reactions in the attack that struck private houses and caused other damage.
